ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AC$, $AB=4$, and $BC=7$. What is the perimeter of $\triangle ABD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AC$,\\
$\therefore AD=CD$,\\
$\therefore BC=BD+CD=BD+AD$,\\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of $\triangle ABD$ $=AB+BD+AD=AB+BC=4+7=\boxed{11}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure, A, B, C form triangle ABC; on the base, B, D, C are on the same straight line, and D is located between B and C; from D upward it is connected to A, and there is another straight line DE passing through D and intersecting side AC at E; at E there is a right-angle symbol, indicating that DE is perpendicular to AC. Then reason: The problem gives that DE is the perpendicular bisector of AC, so point D located on this perpendicular bisector has equal distances to A and C, that is, AD=CD.
